summary.name: Note-taking (Wikipedia)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing note-taking as a practice, covering its history, cognitive psychology, and the linear and non-linear methods used to record information.
use_cases: Understanding handwritten versus laptop note-taking research
Learning Cornell Notes or SQ3R study techniques
Studying the history of notebooks and commonplace books
Organizing information with outlines or mind maps
summary.what_it_does: The article defines note-taking as recording information from sources such as lectures, meetings, and discussions, and traces its history from Ancient Greek hypomnema and Renaissance student notebooks to Locke's commonplace book indexing. It explains the cognitive processes involved and cites studies comparing handwritten and typed notes. It describes linear methods (outlining, sentence method) and non-linear methods (charting, mapping, Cornell Notes, SQ3R, guided notes, card files). It also covers electronic note-taking, including mixed research findings on laptops versus paper.
notable: Covers Cornell Notes, developed by Walter Pauk at Cornell University
Summarizes research on handwritten versus typed or laptop notes
Describes SQ3R and SQ4R reading and note methods
Lists AI-guided note-taking websites such as Turbo A.I., StudyCu, and Stydra
caveats: Encyclopedia article, not a software tool; it names no specific note-taking app as a product to download
Research findings on digital versus handwritten notes are mixed, as the article itself notes
